questions.hint: The \(x\)-coordinate is negative and the \(y\)-coordinate is positive.

steps.explain: A negative \(x\) and positive \(y\) place the point to the left of the \(y\)-axis and above the \(x\)-axis.
This region is Quadrant II.

questions.stem: A point is located 5 units to the left of the origin and 2 units below it. What are its coordinates?
questions.hint: Left of the origin means a negative \(x\); below the origin means a negative \(y\).

steps.explain: 5 units left of the origin gives \(x=-5\).
2 units below the origin gives \(y=-2\).
Combine to state the coordinates.

Coordinates are written (x, y): x is across, y is up or down.

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).
Check the position of the dot against the ordered pair.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).
Check the position of the dot against the ordered pair.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).
Check the position of the dot against the ordered pair.

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).
Check the position of the dot against the ordered pair.

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
Check the position of the dot against the ordered pair.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

questions.stem: Plot the ordered pairs \(\left(3,\ 2\right),\ \left(5,\ 3\right),\ \left(3,\ 4\right),\ \left(1,\ 3\right)\) on a Cartesian plane (axes from 6 to −6) and join the dots with a ruler in the order given. Name the geometrical shape that you have created.
questions.hint: Plot the dots, join them in order, then count the sides and compare their lengths.

steps.explain: Draw a Cartesian plane with axes numbered from 6 to −6. Plot each ordered pair: go across for x, then up or down for y, and put a dot.

steps.explain: So the shape is a rhombus.
Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
An ordered pair is written (x, y): across first, then up or down.
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

questions.stem: Plot the ordered pairs \(\left(-3,\ 1\right),\ \left(-3,\ 5\right),\ \left(-5,\ 5\right),\ \left(-5,\ 1\right)\) on a Cartesian plane (axes from 6 to −6) and join the dots with a ruler in the order given. Name the geometrical shape that you have created.
questions.hint: Plot the dots, join them in order, then count the sides and compare their lengths.

steps.explain: Draw a Cartesian plane with axes numbered from 6 to −6. Plot each ordered pair: go across for x, then up or down for y, and put a dot.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
An ordered pair is written (x, y): across first, then up or down.
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).

questions.stem: Plot the ordered pairs \(\left(-5,\ -2\right),\ \left(-5,\ 2\right),\ \left(-1,\ 6\right),\ \left(4,\ 2\right),\ \left(5,\ -3\right),\ \left(0,\ -6\right)\) on a Cartesian plane (axes from 6 to −6) and join the dots with a ruler in the order given. Name the geometrical shape that you have created.
questions.hint: Plot the dots, join them in order, then count the sides and compare their lengths.

steps.explain: So the shape is a hexagon.
Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
An ordered pair is written (x, y): across first, then up or down.
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

questions.stem: Plot the ordered pairs \(\left(5,\ -1\right),\ \left(5,\ 1\right),\ \left(3,\ 1\right),\ \left(3,\ -1\right)\) on a Cartesian plane (axes from 6 to −6) and join the dots with a ruler in the order given. Name the geometrical shape that you have created.
questions.hint: Plot the dots, join them in order, then count the sides and compare their lengths.

steps.explain: Draw a Cartesian plane with axes numbered from 6 to −6. Plot each ordered pair: go across for x, then up or down for y, and put a dot.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).

questions.stem: Plot the ordered pairs \(\left(1,\ 3\right),\ \left(1,\ 5\right),\ \left(-2,\ 4\right)\) on a Cartesian plane (axes from 6 to −6) and join the dots with a ruler in the order given. Name the geometrical shape that you have created.
questions.hint: Plot the dots, join them in order, then count the sides and compare their lengths.

steps.explain: Draw a Cartesian plane with axes numbered from 6 to −6. Plot each ordered pair: go across for x, then up or down for y, and put a dot.

steps.explain: So the shape is a triangle.
Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
An ordered pair is written (x, y): across first, then up or down.
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

questions.stem: Plot the ordered pairs \(\left(2,\ -1\right),\ \left(1,\ 2\right),\ \left(-2,\ 2\right),\ \left(-3,\ -1\right)\) on a Cartesian plane (axes from 6 to −6) and join the dots with a ruler in the order given. Name the geometrical shape that you have created.
questions.hint: Plot the dots, join them in order, then count the sides and compare their lengths.

steps.explain: Draw a Cartesian plane with axes numbered from 6 to −6. Plot each ordered pair: go across for x, then up or down for y, and put a dot.

steps.explain: The top side (from (−2,2) to (1,2)) and the bottom side (from (−3,−1) to (2,−1)) are both horizontal, so they are parallel but different lengths (3 and 5). The other two sides slope. One pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium.

steps.explain: So the shape is a trapezium.
Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
An ordered pair is written (x, y): across first, then up or down.
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 14: Maps and coordinates

questions.stem: At what point do the diagonals intersect in part a of question 3 (the shape made from \(\left(3,\ 2\right),\ \left(5,\ 3\right),\ \left(3,\ 4\right),\ \left(1,\ 3\right)\))?
questions.hint: The diagonals meet in the middle of the shape.

steps.explain: Plot the rhombus from part a and join the dots.

steps.explain: A shape with 8 sides is an octagon. (Its sides are not all the same length, so it is an irregular octagon.)
Why the other answers are wrong: they swap x and y, or use the wrong sign for a number across or up/down.

keyPoints.note: The Cartesian plane has an x-axis (across) and a y-axis (up and down).
An ordered pair is written (x, y): across first, then up or down.
Go across first (x), then up or down (y).
